hard_gates.evidence: Shared schema-v2 TransportRequest/TransportResponse contract is used by ChatGptNativeMaterializedTransport and the remote worker.

remote_worker/transport_worker.py performs GET/HEAD, response capture, byte counting, checksumming, timing, and error capture only; it contains no identifier resolution, OA/provider selection, scholarly validation, terminal-state assignment, or manifest generation.

Production acquire_one() for PMID 24782981 emitted NEEDS_FETCH for PMC fullTextXML after native transport returned not_materialized; resume_acquire_one() ingested the correlated remote TransportResponse in the same serialized session and completed SUCCESS.
GitHub Actions run 32540936432 completed successfully and returned exact materialized bytes for both live transport checks.
Europe PMC / PMC3995050/fullTextXML, previously blocked by native materialization limits, returned HTTP 200 and 131980 bytes remotely.

Python independently recomputed the raw JATS transport SHA-256 f5be0435...9185, verified it against the transport checksum, extracted/normalized JATS, verified exact article identity, validated the scholarly payload, and wrote final artifact SHA-256 0c637ff8...a8000.
Contract tests prove transport errors cannot yield EXHAUSTED; absent native materialization falls through to remote; uncertain transport remains BLOCKED/NEEDS_FETCH as applicable.
Requests, responses, exact transport payloads, transport checksums, runtime journals/receipts, manifests, GitHub Actions logs/artifact metadata, and portable evidence copies are preserved.

capability_state.note: Prompt 2 proves transport materialization only. Provider support promotion is intentionally deferred to Prompt 3.

discrepancies.description: Prompt 1 stored v0_4.transport as scalar 'chatgpt_native', while Prompt 2 needs structured transport evidence. The controller now migrates the scalar compatibly and retains it as legacy_transport_label.
AcquisitionConfig.want_structured and want_pdf existed in Prompt 1 but did not control runtime policy. Prompt 2 wires both flags into the production acquisition policy.

Initial Prompt 2 registry semantics treated a native no-bytes result as deferred, which prevented remote fallback. Native non-materialization now continues to remote; only a deferred remote response suspends the controller.

The repository still includes the legacy schema-v1 ExternalFetchRequest used by the older tool-mediated provider engine. It is not used by production acquire_one() or the Prompt 2 remote worker. The single-contract guarantee therefore applies to the repaired production acquisition transport path, not every historical compatibility API in the repository.

The connected GitHub API could not enumerate the initial push-triggered run through the available connector action. A same-repository draft PR trigger was added so the live remote run, jobs, logs, and artifacts could be retrieved and preserved. Remote execution remained real GitHub Actions.

The raw Europe PMC transport checksum differs from the final JATS artifact checksum because Python extracts/normalizes the canonical <article> payload. Both hashes and both byte counts are preserved, and Python verifies the raw transport hash before normalization.
